rubric.why: Distance is the total length of the path travelled.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that distance is the total length of the path travelled.

rubric.why: Displacement is the change in position in a specified direction.
rubric.description: Defines displacement as the straight-line change from initial to final position, including direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the straight-line change in position and its direction.

modelAnswer: Distance is the total length of the path travelled by a body.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position in a specified direction.

items.followUp: State Newton’s First Law of Motion.

rubric.why: The law describes what happens to a body when no unbalanced external force acts on it.
rubric.description: States that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform straight-line motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the body's unchanged state of rest or uniform motion.

rubric.why: The law says that a change in this state occurs only when an external unbalanced force acts.
rubric.description: States that a force is required to change the body's state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning an external or unbalanced force as the cause of a change.

modelAnswer: A body remains at rest or continues to move with uniform velocity in a straight line unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.

items.followUp: A body of mass 4 kg moves with a velocity of 3 m/s. Find its momentum.

rubric.why: Momentum is the product of a body's mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Defines momentum as mass multiplied by velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or the relation p = mv.

rubric.why: The SI unit follows from mass multiplied by velocity.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for kg m/s or an equivalent SI unit.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass and velocity of a body: p = mv.
Its SI unit is kilogram metre per second (kg m/s).

items.followUp: State the principle of moments and write its condition for equilibrium.

rubric.why: The principle states that, for a body in equilibrium, the total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment about the same point.
rubric.description: States equality of clockwise and anticlockwise moments in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correctly stating the equality; award 1 mark if the equality is implied but the equilibrium condition or same-point reference is unclear.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a pivot is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.

items.followUp: State the conditions for translational and rotational equilibrium.

rubric.why: Translational equilibrium requires the resultant force on the body to be zero.
rubric.description: States that the net force is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant or net force is zero.

rubric.why: Rotational equilibrium requires the resultant torque to be zero.
rubric.description: States that the net torque or moment is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant moment is zero, or that clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero.
For complete equilibrium, the resultant torque (moment) on it must also be zero.

items.followUp: Define work and state the two forms of mechanical energy.

rubric.why: Energy is defined as the capacity to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy is the capacity or ability to do work.

rubric.why: The two forms of mechanical energy are kinetic and potential energy.
rubric.description: Names both types of mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both kinetic and potential energy.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
The two types of mechanical energy are kinetic energy and potential energy.

items.followUp: Write the formula for the efficiency of a system and express it as a percentage.

rubric.why: Efficiency compares useful output with the input to a system.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful output divided by input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct output-to-input ratio.

rubric.why: Efficiency is commonly expressed as a percentage by multiplying the ratio by 100.
rubric.description: States that the ratio is multiplied by 100% or expressed as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the percentage conversion.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy (or work) to the input energy (or work).

items.followUp: Define pressure and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Pressure is force exerted per unit area.
rubric.description: Defines pressure as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air in the atmosphere acting on surfaces.
rubric.description: Identifies atmospheric pressure as pressure exerted by the atmosphere due to air's weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to the atmosphere or air and its weight/force.

modelAnswer: Atmospheric pressure is the force per unit area exerted by the atmosphere due to the weight of the air above a surface.
